michelle_support: FYI escalation — customer reports p99 TTFB for streaming is ~2.1s but non-streaming p99 ~0.6s. Started after the 2026-03-14 edge rollout. They only see it on browser SSE. Request IDs: rqx_01A2, rqx_01A7. Any quick ideas?

raj_eng: Do we know the client path (SSE vs h2) + region? Also which model?

michelle_support: SSE from EU users (eu-west-1). Model: redwood-1-small. UA: "AcmeWeb/1.2.3". Sample headers + small repro pasted to logs: https://redwood/logs/rqx_01A2 (internal).

alejandro_sre: Noted. We rolled a coalescing tweak on 2026-03-14 that increased `edge_flush_window_ms` from 10 -> 50 in eu-west-1 for better throughput. That would increase first-chunk latency for low-volume SSE clients.

evan_prod: Can we reproduce locally? Try a curl SSE sim: `curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Prefer: streaming" --http2 "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"` and capture first byte time. Also capture edge proxy logs with `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/sse.cap host <edge-ip>` if needed.

michelle_support: Ran the curl sim against eu-west edge. Observed timings: first byte ~2.05s, subsequent chunks steady. Non-streaming call to same model returned first byte ~0.58s. Pasted small log snippet: ```[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] req=rqx_01A2 edge_flush_window_ms=50 first_chunk_delay=2053ms runtime_dispatch=120ms```

raj_eng: Confirms correlation with edge_flush_window_ms bump. For SSE the edge intentionally waits up to the flush window to coalesce small writes into a single packet; that increases TTFB p99. For non-stream we buffer until response ready, so difference is expected.

alejandro_sre: Short-term mitigations: 1) rollback the eu-west rollout of the larger flush window, or 2) add a tenant override that forces small flush window / disable coalesce for this tenant. We can also set a header to force non-streaming fallback `X-Prefer-NonStreaming: 1` from support while we triage.

evan_prod: For longer term we should make coalescing adaptive by client RTT + client type (browser SSE should favor lower flush window). But immediate action: SRE rollback or tenant override.

michelle_support: Customer is asking for ETA. I'll offer a temporary client header to switch to non-streaming and ask SRE to prioritize rollback if it's cheap.

alejandro_sre: I'll roll back the eu-west change now and monitor p99. Rolling back flag: `edge_flush_window_ms=10` for eu-west-1. Estimated 5m to apply and 10m for metric convergence.

deploy-bot: [deployment] rollback started for config=edge-coalesce in eu-west-1 by alejandro_sre. changelist: CL-33921.

raj_eng: After rollback, we should run the curl repro and get p99 numbers and a perf dashboard snapshot (edge/ingress/rtg). Also add a metric for "first_chunk_delay_ms" on edge to surface this faster.

michelle_support: Thanks all — I'll update the customer and patch support ticket with the non-stream header option and ETA. :thumbsup:

alejandro_sre: Rollback complete. Metrics show first_chunk p99 dropped to ~0.65s for affected tenant in eu-west-1 within 12m. Leaving this open for postmortem and follow-up work item to make coalescing adaptive.

michelle_support: Great, closing loop with customer. Will open a short postmortem doc and link it here when ready.

evan_prod: Filing follow-up: make edge coalescing policy adaptive + expose tenant override API. Created GH issue #4729.

michelle_support: Copy. :white_check_mark:
